mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDP components (GDPC1) show a sustained monthly increase of at least 2% over three consecutive months, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days tend to be positive as investors anticipate stronger economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth rate >= 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In a regime of persistent inflation or supply shock, 20-day forward returns do not exceed the 10th percentile of similar non-recession months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the CPIAUCSL index above 3% in the prior month coincides with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as market anticipates higher inflation and rate hikes.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, returns remain negative or flat despite CPIAUCSL exceeding 3%.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 5% (indicated by UNRATE), the S&P 500 20-day forward return becomes negative due to over-optimism about job creation and subsequent policy tightening expectations.
failure_condition: In regimes with structural unemployment or post-crisis normalization, the return is not significantly negative.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 4% suggests supply-side strength that compresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days as profit expectations cool.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from a baseline of zero return.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising home sales (HOUST) above 600K units triggers a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as housing market strength signals consumer confidence.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly average > 600000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns fail to beat the 5th percentile of non-boom periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) and a rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) creates a conflicting dual signal that produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days when both move in opposite directions.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases while CPIAUCSL increases over the same month
failure_condition: Interaction effect is not statistically significant in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate remains persistently below 2% for three consecutive months in a non-recession regime, the S&P 500 60-day forward return tends to be positive as markets anticipate further easing.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for 3 consecutive months and not in recession regime
failure_condition: 60-day returns are flat or negative despite sustained rate low.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in jobless claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 250K for a month is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as it signals labor market stress and potential policy intervention.
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not turn negative in subsequent months with improving labor data.
